data.title: H2 antihistamines (cimetidine, ranitidine, famotidine)
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Antihistamines_

**Class:** H2 receptor antagonists

## Mechanism of action
- Block H2 receptors on gastric parietal cells and on skin blood vessels (part of wheal and flare)
- Cimetidine also has immunomodulatory (blocks suppressor T-cell H2 receptors) and anti-androgenic effects

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Add-on to H1 antihistamines in chronic urticaria (small extra benefit), anaphylaxis adjunct, mastocytosis
- Cimetidine: warts in children (immunomodulatory — evidence weak), hirsutism (anti-androgen), reduces dapsone methaemoglobinaemia

## Dose & formulations
- Famotidine 20–40 mg twice daily; cimetidine 400 mg twice daily (warts 30–40 mg/kg/day)

## Adverse effects
- Generally safe; cimetidine — gynaecomastia, impotence, confusion in elderly, CYP inhibition
- Ranitidine withdrawn worldwide in 2020 (NDMA carcinogen contamination)

## Contraindications
- Hypersensitivity

## Drug interactions
- Cimetidine inhibits CYP1A2, 2D6, 3A4 → raises warfarin, theophylline, phenytoin, lignocaine, doxepin levels

## Pregnancy & lactation
Famotidine considered safe.

## Viva points
- H1 + H2 combination in refractory urticaria
- Cimetidine: interactions, gynaecomastia, warts (immunomodulation)
- Ranitidine withdrawn — NDMA

_Sources: Khopkar (Antihistamines); Wolverton 4e ch.32. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
